title: 16,384 days
detail: Two to the fourteenth power.

title: As old as George Foreman when he won the title back
detail: In 1994, at 45, Foreman became heavyweight champion again, 20 years after he first lost the title.

title: As old as Jack Nicklaus at his last Masters win
detail: In 1986, at 46, Nicklaus won the Masters for a sixth time.

title: As long as Koko the gorilla learned to sign
detail: Koko learned more than 1,000 signs over about 46 years and used them to talk about her feelings and her cats.

title: Four whole years on Jupiter
detail: Jupiter has gone around the Sun four times since day one.

title: As old as Momofuku Ando when he invented instant ramen
detail: He came up with instant noodles in 1958, at 48.

title: As long as some bamboo waits to bloom
detail: Melocanna bamboo in India flowers all at once about every 48 years, then the plants die and start over from seed.
There are 17,576 different three-letter combinations, from AAA to ZZZ.

title: One day for every Peanuts comic strip
detail: Charles Schulz drew 17,897 Peanuts strips over almost 50 years, all by himself.

title: As old as Julia Child when her first cookbook came out
detail: Mastering the Art of French Cooking was published in 1961, when she was 49.

title: Fifty years
detail: Half a century, one day at a time.

title: About five whole new skeletons
detail: Your bones rebuild themselves bit by bit, about every ten years.

title: As long as a big macaw can live
detail: Large macaws can live 50 years or more.

title: As long as Castor's light takes to reach us
detail: Castor, one of the twin stars of Gemini, is about 51 light-years away.

title: About 30 billion miles around the Sun
detail: At about 67,000 miles an hour, Earth never stops moving, and neither have you.

title: As old as Gordie Howe in his last NHL season
detail: Mr. Hockey played all 80 games in 1979-80, at 52.

title: One day for every foot of Kilimanjaro
detail: Africa's tallest mountain rises 19,341 feet.

title: As old as Walt Disney when Disneyland opened
detail: He was 53 when the park opened in July 1955.

title: 20,000 days
detail: Nearly 55 years, and about 2 billion heartbeats.

title: As old as a saguaro cactus when it grows its first arm
detail: Saguaros grow very slowly. Most don't sprout their first arm until they're somewhere between 50 and 75 years old.

title: One day for every foot of Denali
detail: North America's tallest mountain is 20,310 feet high.

title: As old as Dr. Seuss when Green Eggs and Ham came out
detail: He was 56. He wrote it on a bet that he couldn't write a book with only 50 different words.

title: A great great gross
As long as the Arecibo telescope listened to the sky
detail: The giant radio dish in Puerto Rico worked for 57 years, from 1963 to 2020.

title: As old as Anna Sewell when Black Beauty came out
detail: Her only book was published in 1877, when she was 57. It has sold tens of millions of copies.

title: Two whole years on Saturn
detail: Saturn takes about 29½ Earth years to go around the Sun. It's done it twice since day one.

title: As old as Clara Barton when she founded the American Red Cross
detail: She started it in 1881, at 59.

title: Five whole years on Jupiter
detail: Jupiter has gone around the Sun five times since day one.

title: As long as an elephant can live
detail: African elephants can live 60 to 70 years in the wild.

title: 750 full moons
detail: About 750 trips of the Moon through its phases since day one.

title: 22,222 days
detail: Five twos in a row.

title: As long as an African grey parrot can live
detail: African grey parrots can live 60 years or more in a good home, and some learn hundreds of words.

title: As old as Harland Sanders when he started franchising
detail: Colonel Sanders began selling his chicken recipe to restaurants in 1952, at 62.

title: As old as Tolkien when The Lord of the Rings came out
detail: The first volume was published in July 1954, when he was 62.

title: One day for every yard Jerry Rice gained
detail: Jerry Rice caught passes for 22,895 yards, the NFL record by a long way.

title: As old as Diana Nyad when she swam from Cuba to Florida
detail: In 2013, at 64 and on her fifth try, she swam about 110 miles in 53 hours.

title: As old as Laura Ingalls Wilder when her first book came out
detail: Little House in the Big Woods was published in 1932, when she was 65.

title: As long as Aldebaran's light takes to reach us
detail: Aldebaran, the red eye of Taurus the bull, is about 65 light-years away.

title: As long as it took to go from the first airplane to the Moon
detail: The Wright brothers first flew on December 17, 1903. Apollo 11 landed on the Moon 65½ years later.

title: As old as Frank McCourt when Angela's Ashes came out
detail: His first book was published in 1996, when he was 66. It won the Pulitzer Prize.

title: As long as Vin Scully called Dodgers games
detail: He was the voice of the Dodgers for 67 seasons, from 1950 to 2016.

title: 24,680 days
detail: Two, four, six, eight, oh.

title: As old as Frank Lloyd Wright when he designed Fallingwater
detail: He drew the famous house over a waterfall in 1935, at 68.

title: 25,000 days
detail: More than 68 years. Your heart has beaten about 2½ billion times since day one.

title: About half a billion breaths
detail: At about 20,000 breaths a day, the breaths add up to half a billion since day one.

title: As old as Wisdom the albatross when she hatched a chick
detail: Wisdom, a Laysan albatross, hatched a chick in 2021 at about 70, the oldest known wild bird.

title: As old as Benjamin Franklin when he signed the Declaration
detail: He was 70 when he signed it in 1776, the oldest signer.

title: As long as Queen Elizabeth II reigned
detail: She was queen for 70 years and 214 days, from 1952 to 2022.
